rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal models. This experiment tests a multimodal setup with PCA and ResNet50 encoders using concat fusion, which isolates the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploration by testing a standard multimodal configuration while keeping complexity manageable.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieved 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is a logical extension of the previous configuration and helps determine if weighted fusion could yield better results, balancing exploitation of the multimodal direction with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~52.6% accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) with concat fusion, isolating the impact of profile setting. It balances exploration of multiprofile (a key design choice) and builds on prior multimodal success, while keeping RNA/image encoders consistent to attribute performance changes to aggregation/fusion.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings (like config_018) achieve higher accuracy than singleprofile or unimodal models. This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same setup improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion methods. It directly builds on the strong performance of config_018 while exploring a critical design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while maintaining weighted fusion, isolating the impact of aggregation method. This balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a potentially more powerful aggregation technique, which is critical for model performance in multimodal tasks.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6389). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) can further improve performance while keeping the effective multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion setup. This isolates the impact of the image encoder, a critical component, and builds on the strong foundation of the current best configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l encoders achieve high accuracy (0.6352-0.6389). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (the fusion method of the current best config_019) to isolate the impact of aggregation strategy. It balances exploitation of promising components (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l) with exploration of transformer aggregation, which could improve performance over avgpool used in config_019.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.638999). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) could further improve performance, while keeping other components (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) consistent. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and builds on the promising direction of multiprofile and weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (config_031: 0.6776). This experiment tests combining scvi_n200 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation, which could further improve performance by leveraging advanced vision models and complex feature interactions. It isolates the impact of image encoder quality and aggregation method on top of a strong RNA encoder and fusion strategy.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt RNA encoder (a more advanced model) could further improve performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while keeping other components consistent. This is the best use of the final experiment to explore a promising direction with minimal changes.
